text.p: Base metals stole the focus from other commodities in overnight trading as zinc, aluminium, copper and nickel shot up but then struggled to hold gains.
Zinc showed the most stamina, extending Monday's gains to Reach a 4-1/2 year high above $1,250 per tonne on the London metal Exchange (LME).
It was helped up by a fall of 1,400 tonnes in LME-supervised warehouse stocks and later in the day resisted a wave of profit-taking that swept the London metals market.

But the profit taking completely eroded strong gains in aluminium which had jumped to a 14-month high above $1,700 per tonne amid concern over Russian supply. It ended the London day at $1,685, down $5 from Monday.

Copper failed to hold on to a nine-month high of $2,420 reached in morning trade, slipping lower before ending at $2,395 per tonne. Nickel, meanwhile, tumbled below the $8,300 level as strike fears eased at Russia's Arctic metals complex at Norilsk.
Lead edged below the $700 level in kerb trading and ended at $697, a $3 decline. Cash/threes remained in backwardation.
Brokers GNI said in a market commentary: "there is no reason not to plump for a global boom (in base metals) at some stage in the next few months."
A report by technical analysts Wavetrack said zinc could surpass a medium-term target of $1,550 by early 1998. It also predicted a bull market in nickel.

COMEX and NYMEX were steady at lower levels at the New York midday, after some early fund selling ran into support from the trade. A recovery in the U.S. dollar and some signs of a return to stability in U.S. bond and stock markets had lowered some of the incentive for investors in precious metals, traders said. Comex April gold was down $2.50 at $361.30 at midday after seeing a $364.50-360.20 range but declined to $360.1 later in the session . In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $358.50/359.00, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $359.40 and the New York close Monday at $361.70/20.

CBOT wheat futures were sharply up at midday on fund buying and concerns about wet weather in the U.S. midwest. Prices were three to six cents per bushel higher, with March up 5-1/2 at $3.78-1/2 by midday, but slipping back to $3.1, two off on the session in late trading

NYMEX crude was near its highs after a day or rallys and profit-taking fuelled by technical strength and short covering ahead of weekly oil inventory data. "People are going to sell rallys in this market, plus you have a lot of people who want to flatten positions ahead of the APIs," said a New York dealer. At 2030 GMT, April crude was up 39 cents at $20.64 a barrel after highs of around $20.89. The American Petroleum Institute (API) will release oil inventory data for the week ended February 28 Tuesday evening.
